//: Which model a LEVEL means, per vendor. This is the only place a model name appears in the collaboration layer: tasks, delegations and the rules speak in levels (L0..L3) and in the stable `ref` below, so a vendor shipping a new model is an edit here and nothing else. Models come and go — the level ladder does not.
//levels: A level is HOW HARD the work is, never who does it. `rank` orders them and nothing reads the name. A task classified above a model's `max_level` escalates to the next rung instead of being handed to it; a task below `level` does not need that rung, and taking it anyway is how everything quietly runs on the most expensive model.
//ref: `ref` is the stable name (`sonnet`, `terra`, `gemini-pro-high`) that rules, delegations and the journal use. `id` is the vendor's own model id, which changes under you. Two rungs may share one `id` with different `effort` — that is why the key is `ref` and not `id`.
//verified: How much the `id` beside it can be trusted. `catalog` — checked against the vendor's own catalog file on this machine, and `collab doctor` re-checks it and reports drift. `owner` — the owner confirmed it; there is no catalog here to check against. `unverified` — copied from documentation and never confirmed on this machine; do not rely on it until somebody has.
//adapters: Nothing here starts anything. Choosing and launching a model is the lead session's own doing; this file is what it chooses FROM, and the journal records what it says it chose. The layer cannot verify which model actually ran.

L0.summary: Mechanical. A known answer or a repetitive edit: rename, move, collect, summarise. No judgement, nothing to get architecturally wrong.

L1.summary: Ordinary. Clear local work in one area, verifiable by a test or a look. This is the default, and most days most work is this.

L2.summary: Hard. Several modules, state or concurrency, an ambiguous requirement, a wide regression surface, or a change whose cost of being wrong is real.

L3.summary: Critical. Irreversible, or touching credentials, privacy, payments or user data; a migration; or a question two strong models already disagree about.

//review_risk_floor: Where the level a task DECLARES stops being its own business. An action the policy table classifies as one of these cannot have a review risk below the level named here, however small the diff looks — one line in auth is the case this exists for. The keys are action classes from policy.json; the values are levels above.

anthropic.note: Model ids come from the harness, which has no catalog file to read; `doctor` reports them as unverifiable rather than ok.

openai.note: The Codex CLI keeps its own catalog, so these ids are checkable — and they do drift: gpt-reserve and codex-auto-review appeared between two weeks of documentation and 2026-09-15.

google.note: The npm package @google/gemini-cli is dead for this purpose — Google cut free/Pro/Ultra individual access to it on 2026-06-18. The working client is Antigravity CLI (`agy`), which has no local catalog file for `doctor` to check automatically; `agy models` was run by hand on 2026-09-15 and its output copied below, with a real headless call confirmed against collab's own whoami on the cheapest rung (gemini-3.6-flash-low).

minimax.note: There is no catalog file here to check against, so `doctor` reports this vendor as unverifiable rather than ok. `minimax-dev --check` (2026-10-02) confirmed the one thing it can: the launcher accepts the route minimax-coding-plan/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview. That is the launcher agreeing with a request, NOT an upstream catalog confirming the id, so it is recorded as unverified and nobody should read more into it.

xai.note: The ids below come from the account's own saved catalog on disk, dated 2026-09-18, and nothing else. Refreshing it failed with 401 — the saved login is expired — so `doctor` reports this vendor as unverifiable rather than ok, and neither id is claimed to be reachable today. Nobody has read the account's credentials to check it, and the price, the context width and what each id can do are deliberately left blank rather than guessed.

models.note: Mechanical search, collection and summaries. Cheap enough that using it for L0 work is the whole point.
The default for ordinary work and for orchestration itself. Reaching past it needs a named reason, not a feeling that the task looks big.
Architecture, cross-module reasoning, hard debugging — where tying evidence to code is the work.
Rare by design: a foundational change, a long migration, or arbitrating a disagreement Opus could not settle.
Mechanical checks in a repository the layer can verify: a build, a diff, a grep with a verdict.
Ordinary implementation and ordinary review. Most reviews belong here, not on the top rung.
Deep review and harder implementation — the workhorse for work that would hurt if a defect got through.
Not the default reviewer. One run costs a large share of the owner's five-hour window, so it is asked for by name, with the price said out loud first.
Previous generation, kept only as the last fallback when a rung is unavailable. Holds no rung of its own.
Bulk mechanical passes over many files. Confirmed live 2026-09-15 via `agy models` and a real whoami call through collab.
Ordinary wide or visual analysis — many files, several screens, long logs. Confirmed live 2026-09-15 via `agy models`.
Holds no rung of its own — a real step between flash-medium and pro-low, kept only as the fallback pro-low degrades to. Confirmed live 2026-09-15 via `agy models`.
Independent deep analysis across a large context, where being a different vendor is the point. Confirmed live 2026-09-15 via `agy models`; runs on the owner's Google AI Pro subscription.

The critical rung — arbitration and the hardest independent review. Confirmed live 2026-09-15 via `agy models`; runs on the owner's Google AI Pro subscription, with overage credits at Google's Enterprise Agent Platform pricing above the plan's baseline quota.

Ceiling L1 until a model call has been watched: a preview route nobody ran through the journal is not trusted with harder work. Pinned preview route for bounded implementation. No alternate MiniMax route or GPT fallback is authorized. If the route fails, stop and report to the owner; never switch models automatically. Launcher validation is confirmed; independent upstream catalog verification is pending.

Ordinary implementation and ordinary review on a different vendor, which is where its value is: an error that does not correlate with the author's. The id was read out of the account's own saved catalog on disk, dated 2026-09-18, and from nowhere else; the login that would confirm it is expired (refresh 401), so this is unverified twice over — nobody has watched this model run, and it may not be reachable on that account at all. Maturity is `unverified` rather than a guess, and no cost, context width or capability is recorded: those are exactly the fields a registry starts lying in. There is no fallback to another vendor's model.

Ceiling L2, not L3: L3 is the work whose miss costs most, and this model has not been seen to run (login 401). The deeper rung — independent review, cross-module reasoning, the work whose cost of being wrong is real. The level says how hard the work has to be to belong here; it says nothing about what this account can reach. Same evidence, same absence of it: an id from a saved catalog dated 2026-09-18, an expired login, no live call, no vendor catalog to drift against. A review on this rung still runs read-only with subagents off and no permission bypass — that is a property of the invocation the owner starts, not a limit of the model or of the CLI.
